## 2024-05-18 - Missing Security Headers in Angular SSR Express Server
**Vulnerability:** The default Express server generated by Angular SSR does not implement standard security headers (e.g., `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Strict-Transport-Security`) and leaves the `X-Powered-By: Express` header enabled, creating a defense-in-depth gap and leaking framework information.
**Learning:** Framework boilerplates prioritize functionality over security hardening. Even for server-side rendering endpoints, explicit middleware must be added to enforce HTTP security headers.
**Prevention:** Always audit and harden default server setups generated by frameworks. Incorporate security middleware (like Helmet or custom headers) in the base server configuration template.
